title: Resident Stack Finalization: Continual Scheduler And Adaptive Resource Governor
objective: Finalize LeafOS as a resident live agentic stack that continually executes durable queued work, accepts light operator input, targets productive CPU and GPU utilization, and preserves foreground workstation responsiveness.
constraints: Reuse the existing inlet, version-2 queue, worker lease, journal, validation, and checkpoint authority.
Treat all downloaded and locally available models in this instance as the stack.
Use 80 percent CPU and 90 percent GPU as adaptive productive targets, not synthetic load requirements.
Reduce dispatch pressure for recent operator input, responsiveness loss, memory pressure, thermal pressure, or provider degradation.
Do not give TUI renderers shell, filesystem, queue-file, or policy-file authority.
Do not generate unbounded work without project boundaries and a renewable budget.
Do not display or persist private model chain-of-thought.
acceptance: The resident stack accepts durable tasks while another task is executing.
Eligible tasks continue across TUI disconnects and supervisor restarts without duplicate claims.
Idle productive windows target approximately 80 percent CPU and 90 percent GPU while interactive and pressure profiles preserve foreground headroom.
Every resource decision has a stable reason code and visible current versus target values.
Automatic queue refill is derived from validated evidence and bounded by time, iteration, failure, and change budgets.
The provider remains warm, uses bounded restart backoff, and never silently substitutes mock output.
Both TUI renderers expose authenticated typed controls for profile, targets, budget, pause, resume, drain, and stop.
Generic projects pass 4-minute, 8-minute, and 64-minute resident-stack demonstrations with validated iterative improvements.
